headline: Startup sues Apple in India over NameDrop contact sharing
pages: GG Technologies, the Santa Monica startup behind the StayTouch app, is suing Apple in India, claiming the NameDrop feature in iOS infringes its patent. NameDrop lets users share contact details by holding phones close together. In a 781-page filing in the Bombay High Court, the company seeks 15 billion rupees, about $162 million, and an injunction. It also wants Apple barred from selling or importing iPhones and Apple Watches with NameDrop in India. The company says it got its Indian patent in July 2024 and filed the suit in October after mediation failed in September.

It also sued Apple in the US in April, and the International Trade Commission opened an investigation in August that could lead to an import ban. Apple did not respond to a request for comment, and no hearing has been listed. Why it matters: India is a fast-growing market and manufacturing hub for Apple. Source: TechCrunch.
